intro: Welcome back! You already know was/were + -ing for something in progress at a past time: At 8 last night I was cooking. Now you'll use it to tell stories: the past continuous sets the scene, and the past simple tells what happened, joined with when and while: I was cooking when the phone rang.
teachingNotes: Recap only: the learner knows was/were + -ing from a2-past-continuous-intro (an action in progress at a past time) and the past simple. Don't re-teach the form; fix it briefly when it slips, especially after while (*'While I was walk home' → 'was walking'; *'While I walking' → 'I was walking').

Core idea: in a story the past continuous is the background (the longer action already in progress, the scene: It was raining, people were waiting) and the past simple is the main event (a short, finished action that happens in the middle of it or moves the story on). Picture a long bar (was cooking) with a short point on it (the phone rang). The #1 error is putting the short event in the continuous too (*'I was watching TV when the phone was ringing' → 'rang'). Indonesian marks neither with tense (Saat saya sedang menonton TV, telepon berbunyi), so learners copy 'sedang' onto both verbs or drop the tense altogether (*'Yesterday at 8 I watch TV' → 'Yesterday at 8 I was watching TV').

when / while: Indonesian 'saat/ketika' covers both. Teach the clear pattern: when + past simple for the short event (… when the phone rang); while + was/were + -ing for the longer action (While I was walking home, I saw Rina). Either clause can come first; use a comma when the when/while clause comes first. 'while' is not followed by a short single event in the past simple (*'while the phone rang'). 'When I was cooking, …' is also correct English: say so if asked, but never test sentences where both when and while fit. 'during' goes before a noun (during the meeting), never before subject + verb (*'during I was cooking').

Two actions at the same time: while + past continuous in both parts (While Sari was cooking, her husband was washing the dishes). Contrast with one event after another: past simple in both parts (When the film ended, we went home = first the film ended, then we went home). 'When I arrived, Rina was making tea' (already in the middle) vs 'When I arrived, Rina made some tea' (after I arrived) can be shown, but test only clear cases.

Stories: set the scene with the past continuous (It was a rainy Monday. Everyone was waiting for the KRL.), then tell the events in order in the past simple (Suddenly the train stopped. A man shouted.). Useful words: suddenly (tiba-tiba), then, after that. Ask the learner two questions: 'What was happening?' (was/were + -ing) and 'What happened?' (past simple).

Limits: no past perfect (had + past participle), no 'used to', no passive, no 'as' as a time linker. Verbs like know, want, like and need usually stay in the simple form (*'I was knowing'); just say so if it comes up, don't go deeper.

keyPoints.title: Background and main event
keyPoints.explanation: In a story, the past continuous (was/were + -ing) is the background: a longer action that was already in progress. The past simple is the main event: a short, finished action that happened in the middle of it. The short event stays in the past simple: I was watching TV when the phone rang (not 'was ringing'). A past time still needs a past form: Yesterday at 8 I was watching TV (not 'I watch').

examples.en: I was watching TV when the phone rang.
examples.id: Saya sedang menonton TV ketika telepon berbunyi.

examples.en: Budi was driving to the office when his car broke down.
examples.id: Budi sedang menyetir ke kantor ketika mobilnya mogok.

examples.en: Yesterday at 8 I was watching TV.

id.title: Latar dan kejadian utama
id.explanation: Dalam cerita, past continuous (was/were + -ing) adalah latarnya: kegiatan yang lebih panjang dan sudah sedang berlangsung. Past simple adalah kejadian utamanya: kegiatan singkat dan selesai yang terjadi di tengah-tengahnya. Kejadian singkat tetap memakai past simple: I was watching TV when the phone rang (bukan 'was ringing'). Waktu lampau tetap butuh bentuk lampau: Yesterday at 8 I was watching TV (bukan 'I watch').

keyPoints.title: when + short event, while + long action
keyPoints.explanation: Indonesian uses saat/ketika for both; English chooses by the length of the action. when + past simple introduces the short event: We were having dinner when the lights went out. while + was/were + -ing introduces the long action: While I was walking home, I saw Rina (not 'While I was walk'). Either part can come first; put a comma after the when/while part when it comes first.

examples.en: We were having dinner when the lights went out.
examples.id: Kami sedang makan malam ketika lampu mati.

examples.en: While I was walking home, I saw Rina.
examples.id: Saat saya sedang berjalan pulang, saya melihat Rina.

examples.en: Sari fell asleep while she was watching the film.
examples.id: Sari tertidur saat sedang menonton film.

id.title: when + kejadian singkat, while + kegiatan panjang
id.explanation: Bahasa Indonesia memakai saat/ketika untuk keduanya; bahasa Inggris memilih berdasarkan panjang kegiatannya. when + past simple untuk kejadian singkat: We were having dinner when the lights went out. while + was/were + -ing untuk kegiatan panjang: While I was walking home, I saw Rina (bukan 'While I was walk'). Bagian mana pun boleh di depan; pakai koma setelah bagian when/while kalau bagian itu di depan.

keyPoints.title: Same time, one after another, and stories
keyPoints.explanation: Two long actions at the same time → while + past continuous in both parts: While Sari was cooking, her husband was washing the dishes. One event after another → past simple in both: When the film ended, we went home. A story often starts with the scene in the past continuous, then tells the events in the past simple.

examples.en: While Sari was cooking, her husband was washing the dishes.
examples.id: Saat Sari sedang memasak, suaminya sedang mencuci piring.

examples.en: When the film ended, we went home.
It was raining and everyone was waiting for the bus. Suddenly a man shouted.
examples.id: Sedang hujan dan semua orang sedang menunggu bus. Tiba-tiba seorang laki-laki berteriak.

id.title: Bersamaan, berurutan, dan bercerita
id.explanation: Dua kegiatan panjang yang bersamaan → while + past continuous di kedua bagian: While Sari was cooking, her husband was washing the dishes. Satu kejadian setelah yang lain → past simple di keduanya: When the film ended, we went home. Cerita sering dimulai dengan latar dalam past continuous, lalu kejadian-kejadiannya dalam past simple.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the right form of 'stop': I was taking a shower when the water suddenly ___.
assessment.rubric: Correct: stopped (the short event that happened in the middle of the shower → past simple). 'was stopping' = 30 (the short event doesn't take -ing). 'stoped' = 70 (spelling: double the p). 'stops' or 'stop' = 20 (present).

assessment.prompt: Complete with the right form of 'drive': Pak Hasan ___ to the office when he saw the accident on the toll road.
assessment.rubric: Correct: was driving (the longer background action, already in progress when he saw the accident). 'drove' = 40 (past, but the driving was in progress). 'were driving' = 50 (Pak Hasan = he → was). 'was drive' = 40 (missing -ing). 'is driving' = 20.

assessment.prompt: Complete with when or while: The meeting was going well ___ the projector suddenly broke.
assessment.rubric: Correct: when ('the projector broke' is a short event in the past simple → when). 'while' = 0 (while goes with a longer action in progress, was/were + -ing).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: While I was walk to the KRL station, I dropped my phone.
acceptableAnswers: while i was walking to the krl station i dropped my phone
i dropped my phone while i was walking to the krl station
assessment.rubric: Correct: While I was walking to the KRL station, I dropped my phone (after while: was + -ing). 'While I walking' = 40 (missing was). 'While I walked' = 50. 'I was dropping my phone' = 40 (the short event stays in the past simple). Unchanged = 0. Missing comma: no penalty.

assessment.prompt: Translate: Saat Rina sedang memasak, anak-anaknya sedang bermain di kamar mereka.
acceptableAnswers: while rina was cooking her children were playing in their room
while rina was cooking her kids were playing in their room
her children were playing in their room while rina was cooking
her kids were playing in their room while rina was cooking
when rina was cooking her children were playing in their room
when rina was cooking her kids were playing in their room
while rina was cooking her children were playing in their bedroom
while rina was cooking her kids were playing in their bedroom
assessment.rubric: Correct: While Rina was cooking, her children were playing in their room (two long actions at the same time → was/were + -ing in both parts; 'When Rina was cooking' is also fine). 'her children played' = 60 (both actions were in progress). 'her children was playing' = 60 (children = they → were). 'Rina is cooking' = 30 (present). 'While Rina cooking' = 50 (missing was). 'in her room' = 80.

assessment.prompt: Complete the story with the right form of 'knock': 'It was a quiet evening. It was raining, and the street was empty. I was reading on the terrace when someone ___ on the gate.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: knocked (the scene is in the past continuous; the main event that happens in the middle of it → past simple). 'was knocking' = 30. 'knock' or 'knocks' = 20. 'knoked' = 70 (spelling).

assessment.prompt: Join the two sentences with when: I was having lunch. My boss called me.
acceptableAnswers: i was having lunch when my boss called me
when my boss called me i was having lunch
my boss called me when i was having lunch
i was having lunch when my boss called
assessment.rubric: Correct: I was having lunch when my boss called me (when + the short event). 'when my boss was calling me' = 40 (the short event stays in the past simple). 'I had lunch when my boss called me' = 50 (changes the meaning: the lunch was in progress). 'while my boss called me' = 30. Missing comma in 'When my boss called me, I was having lunch' = no penalty.

blocks.text:
Quick recap: **was/were + -ing** (the past continuous) = an action **in progress** at a time in the past: *At 8 last night I was cooking.* The **past simple** (*cooked, went, rang*) = a **finished** action.

In a story, the two work together:
- **Background** (*latar*): the longer action that was already happening, the scene → **past continuous**: *I was cooking dinner.*
- **Main event** (*kejadian utama*): the short thing that happened in the middle of it → **past simple**: *The phone rang.*

Put them together: **I was cooking dinner when the phone rang.** Picture a **long bar** (the cooking, from 7:00 to 7:45) with a **short point** on it (the phone rang at 7:20). The cooking started before the call, and it wasn't finished when the phone rang.

id.text:
Ingat lagi: **was/were + -ing** (past continuous) = kegiatan yang **sedang berlangsung** pada suatu waktu di masa lalu: *At 8 last night I was cooking.* **Past simple** (*cooked, went, rang*) = kegiatan yang **sudah selesai**.

Dalam cerita, keduanya bekerja sama:
- **Latar** (*background*): kegiatan yang lebih panjang dan sudah sedang terjadi, suasananya → **past continuous**: *I was cooking dinner.*
- **Kejadian utama** (*main event*): hal singkat yang terjadi di tengah-tengahnya → **past simple**: *The phone rang.*

Gabungkan: **I was cooking dinner when the phone rang.** Bayangkan sebuah **garis panjang** (memasak, dari jam 7.00 sampai 7.45) dengan sebuah **titik pendek** di atasnya (telepon berbunyi jam 7.20). Memasaknya sudah dimulai sebelum telepon itu, dan belum selesai waktu telepon berbunyi.

rows.note: the weather is part of the scene → past continuous

id.note: cuaca adalah bagian dari latar → past continuous

blocks.text: The short event stays in the **past simple**, even inside a *was … -ing* sentence: *I was watching TV when the phone **was ringing*** ✗ → **when the phone rang** ✓. Indonesian gives no clue (*Saat saya sedang menonton TV, telepon berbunyi*: no tense on either verb), so ask yourself: which action was **long** (was/were + -ing) and which was **short** (past simple)? And a past time still needs a past form: *Yesterday at 8 I watch TV* ✗ → **Yesterday at 8 I was watching TV** ✓.

id.text: Kejadian singkat tetap memakai **past simple**, walaupun ada *was … -ing* di kalimat yang sama: *I was watching TV when the phone **was ringing*** ✗ → **when the phone rang** ✓. Bahasa Indonesia tidak memberi petunjuk (*Saat saya sedang menonton TV, telepon berbunyi*: kedua kata kerjanya tidak berubah), jadi tanyakan pada dirimu: kegiatan mana yang **panjang** (was/were + -ing) dan mana yang **singkat** (past simple)? Dan waktu lampau tetap butuh bentuk lampau: *Yesterday at 8 I watch TV* ✗ → **Yesterday at 8 I was watching TV** ✓.

blocks.prompt: Dimas was taking a nap when someone ___ the doorbell.
blocks.explain: Taking a nap is the long background action (was taking). Ringing the doorbell is the short event in the middle of it → past simple: rang. 'was ringing' puts the short event in the continuous, and 'rings' is present.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Dimas was taking a nap when someone ___ the doorbell.
id.explain: Tidur siang adalah kegiatan latar yang panjang (was taking). Membunyikan bel adalah kejadian singkat di tengahnya → past simple: rang. 'was ringing' membuat kejadian singkat memakai bentuk continuous, dan 'rings' itu bentuk sekarang.

blocks.text:
Indonesian uses one word, *saat* or *ketika*, for both. English usually chooses by the **length** of the action that comes after it:
- **when + past simple** → the **short** event: *I was cooking **when** the phone **rang**.*
- **while + was/were + -ing** → the **long** action in progress: ***While** I **was walking** home, I saw Rina.*

**while** means 'during the time that' (*selama* / *sementara*), so it needs a long action: *while the phone rang* ✗. After **while**, keep **was/were** and the **-ing**: *While I was walk home* ✗, *While I walking home* ✗ → **While I was walking home** ✓.

Either part can come first. When the *when/while* part comes **first**, put a **comma** after it: ***While I was walking home,** I saw Rina.* When it comes second, no comma: *I saw Rina **while** I was walking home.*

id.text:
Bahasa Indonesia memakai satu kata, *saat* atau *ketika*, untuk keduanya. Bahasa Inggris biasanya memilih berdasarkan **panjang** kegiatan yang mengikutinya:
- **when + past simple** → kejadian yang **singkat**: *I was cooking **when** the phone **rang**.*
- **while + was/were + -ing** → kegiatan **panjang** yang sedang berlangsung: ***While** I **was walking** home, I saw Rina.*

**while** artinya 'selama' / 'sementara', jadi butuh kegiatan yang panjang: *while the phone rang* ✗. Setelah **while**, tetap pakai **was/were** dan **-ing**: *While I was walk home* ✗, *While I walking home* ✗ → **While I was walking home** ✓.

Bagian mana pun boleh di depan. Kalau bagian *when/while* ada **di depan**, beri **koma** setelahnya: ***While I was walking home,** I saw Rina.* Kalau di belakang, tanpa koma: *I saw Rina **while** I was walking home.*

rows.en: We were having dinner when the lights went out.
rows.id: Kami sedang makan malam ketika lampu mati.

rows.en: While Pak Hasan was giving his presentation, his phone rang.
rows.id: Saat Pak Hasan sedang presentasi, HP-nya berbunyi.
rows.note: while + long action (was giving), comma after it

id.note: while + kegiatan panjang (was giving), koma setelahnya

rows.en: Sari fell asleep while she was watching the film.
rows.id: Sari tertidur saat sedang menonton film.

id.note: bagian while di belakang → tanpa koma

rows.en: Budi hurt his knee while he was playing futsal.
rows.id: Lutut Budi cedera saat dia sedang bermain futsal.
rows.note: hurt → hurt (the same in the past)

blocks.text: You'll also hear **when** before a long action: *When I was a student, …*, *When I was cooking, …*. That's correct too, so don't be surprised. But for the long action, **while + -ing** is the clearer choice, and for the **short** event only **when** works. And **during** is different: it goes before a **noun** (*during the meeting*, *during the holiday*), not before a whole sentence: *during I was cooking* ✗ → **while I was cooking** ✓.

id.text: Kamu juga akan mendengar **when** sebelum kegiatan panjang: *When I was a student, …*, *When I was cooking, …*. Itu juga benar, jadi jangan bingung. Tapi untuk kegiatan panjang, **while + -ing** adalah pilihan yang lebih jelas, dan untuk kejadian **singkat** hanya **when** yang bisa. Lalu **during** itu berbeda: dipakai sebelum **kata benda** (*during the meeting* = selama rapat, *during the holiday*), bukan sebelum kalimat lengkap: *during I was cooking* ✗ → **while I was cooking** ✓.

options: While I was wait for the KRL, I read the news.
While I waiting for the KRL, I read the news.
While I was waiting for the KRL, I read the news.
blocks.explain: After while comes the long action with was/were + -ing: While I was waiting. 'was wait' drops the -ing, and 'I waiting' drops was.

id.explain: Setelah while ada kegiatan panjang dengan was/were + -ing: While I was waiting. 'was wait' kehilangan -ing, dan 'I waiting' kehilangan was.

material.title: At the same time, or one after another?

blocks.text:
**Two long actions at the same time** → **while** + past continuous in **both** parts: ***While** Sari **was cooking**, her husband **was washing** the dishes.* Both were in progress together, like two long bars side by side.

**One event after another** → past simple in both parts: ***When** the film **ended**, we **went** home.* First the film ended, then we went home.

So the tense changes the story. Compare:
- *When I arrived, Rina **was making** tea.* → she was already in the middle of making tea.
- *When I arrived, Rina **made** some tea.* → I arrived first, then she made tea.

id.text:
**Dua kegiatan panjang yang bersamaan** → **while** + past continuous di **kedua** bagian: ***While** Sari **was cooking**, her husband **was washing** the dishes.* Keduanya sedang berlangsung bersama, seperti dua garis panjang yang berdampingan.

**Satu kejadian setelah yang lain** → past simple di kedua bagian: ***When** the film **ended**, we **went** home.* Filmnya selesai dulu, lalu kami pulang.

Jadi bentuk kata kerjanya mengubah ceritanya. Bandingkan:
- *When I arrived, Rina **was making** tea.* → dia sudah sedang membuat teh (sebelum saya datang).
- *When I arrived, Rina **made** some tea.* → saya datang dulu, lalu dia membuat teh.

rows.en: While I was studying, my brother was playing games.
rows.id: Saat saya sedang belajar, saudara laki-lakiku sedang bermain game.

blocks.prompt: When Budi came home, his children ___ their homework. (They started before he came and were still in the middle of it.)
blocks.explain: The homework was already in progress when Budi came → were doing (children = they → were). 'did' would mean they started after he came, and 'do' is present.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: When Budi came home, his children ___ their homework. (Mereka mulai sebelum dia datang dan masih di tengah-tengahnya.)
id.explain: PR-nya sudah sedang dikerjakan ketika Budi datang → were doing (children = they → were). 'did' berarti mereka baru mulai setelah dia datang, dan 'do' itu bentuk sekarang.

blocks.text:
A story in English often starts with the **scene** in the past continuous, then moves to the **events** in the past simple, one after another. Words like **suddenly** (*tiba-tiba*), **then** and **after that** help.

*It was a rainy Monday morning. I was standing on a crowded KRL, and everyone was looking at their phones.* → the scene (past continuous)
*Suddenly the train stopped. The lights went out, and a baby started to cry. After ten minutes, the train moved again.* → the events (past simple)

The scene answers **What was happening?**; the events answer **What happened?**

id.text:
Cerita dalam bahasa Inggris sering dimulai dengan **latar** dalam past continuous, lalu pindah ke **kejadian-kejadian** dalam past simple, satu per satu. Kata seperti **suddenly** (*tiba-tiba*), **then** (*lalu*) dan **after that** (*setelah itu*) membantu.

*It was a rainy Monday morning. I was standing on a crowded KRL, and everyone was looking at their phones.* → latarnya (past continuous)
*Suddenly the train stopped. The lights went out, and a baby started to cry. After ten minutes, the train moved again.* → kejadiannya (past simple)

Latar menjawab **What was happening?** (*Apa yang sedang terjadi?*); kejadian menjawab **What happened?** (*Apa yang terjadi?*).

rows.en: It was a rainy Monday morning.
rows.id: Saat itu Senin pagi yang hujan.
rows.note: scene: was is the past of to be

id.note: latar: was adalah bentuk lampau to be

rows.en: Everyone was looking at their phones.
rows.id: Semua orang sedang melihat HP mereka.

rows.en: After ten minutes, the train moved again.
rows.id: Setelah sepuluh menit, keretanya jalan lagi.

blocks.text: To tell your own story, answer two questions: **What was happening?** (was/were + -ing: *I was waiting for an ojek*) and **What happened?** (past simple: *Suddenly it started to rain*). Don't put every verb in the -ing form: a story with only *was … -ing* has a scene but no events.

id.text: Untuk menceritakan kisahmu sendiri, jawab dua pertanyaan: **What was happening?** (was/were + -ing: *I was waiting for an ojek*) dan **What happened?** (past simple: *Suddenly it started to rain*). Jangan memakai -ing untuk semua kata kerja: cerita yang isinya hanya *was … -ing* punya latar tapi tidak punya kejadian.

blocks.prompt: In the KRL story above, which sentence is a main event?
options: I was standing on a crowded KRL.
Everyone was looking at their phones.
blocks.explain: 'A baby started to cry' is a short thing that happened (past simple), so it's an event. The other two (was/were + -ing) describe the scene.

id.prompt: Di cerita KRL di atas, kalimat mana yang merupakan kejadian utama?
id.explain: 'A baby started to cry' adalah hal singkat yang terjadi (past simple), jadi itu kejadian. Dua kalimat lainnya (was/were + -ing) menggambarkan latar.

id.note: Pelajaran 11 menit untuk pemula, seluruhnya dalam bahasa Inggris. Bagian tengah tentang when dan while serta past simple + past continuous bersama cocok dengan pelajaran ini; bagian awalnya mengulang was/were + -ing.

id.intro: Selamat datang lagi! Kamu sudah tahu was/were + -ing untuk kegiatan yang sedang berlangsung pada suatu waktu di masa lalu: At 8 last night I was cooking. Sekarang kamu memakainya untuk bercerita: past continuous membangun latarnya, dan past simple menceritakan apa yang terjadi, dihubungkan dengan when dan while: I was cooking when the phone rang.
suggestedQuestions: Kapan pakai when, dan kapan pakai while?
Kenapa 'when the phone was ringing' salah?
Boleh bilang 'When I was cooking' sebagai ganti 'While I was cooking'?
Bagaimana cara memulai cerita dalam bahasa Inggris?

assessment.pcs-1: Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari 'stop': I was taking a shower when the water suddenly ___.
assessment.pcs-2: Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari 'drive': Pak Hasan ___ to the office when he saw the accident on the toll road.
assessment.pcs-3: Lengkapi dengan when atau while: The meeting was going well ___ the projector suddenly broke.
assessment.pcs-4: Perbaiki kesalahannya: While I was walk to the KRL station, I dropped my phone.
assessment.pcs-5: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Inggris: Saat Rina sedang memasak, anak-anaknya sedang bermain di kamar mereka.
assessment.pcs-6: Lengkapi ceritanya dengan bentuk yang tepat dari 'knock': 'It was a quiet evening. It was raining, and the street was empty. I was reading on the terrace when someone ___ on the gate.'
assessment.pcs-7: Gabungkan kedua kalimat dengan when: I was having lunch. My boss called me.
